plate.prompt: A richly detailed ink-line and watercolor painting, a complete scene painted edge to edge, with no border, frame, vignette, torn paper edge or blank paper showing. Match the attached reference in finish and quality: fine confident linework, many layered washes, realistic light, shadow and water reflections, deep saturated Florida Everglades color (mangrove green, clear green-blue water, warm sunrise orange). Crisp focus and a great deal of small true-to-life detail, like a plate in a premium illustrated fishing handbook. One obvious subject, so it still reads at thumbnail size. No text, letters, numbers, symbols, logos, brand names or signatures anywhere. Any person is seen from behind or as hands only, never a face. Scene: {{line}}

items.line: an open clear-lidded tackle tray on the weathered wooden deck of a flats skiff at sunrise, seen from above at a slight angle: in its compartments an orange-and-white popping cork, a gold weedless spoon, round jig heads, soft-plastic paddle tails in chartreuse and pink, circle hooks, egg sinkers and a spool of clear leader, every piece drawn accurately with highlights and tiny shadows; a rod butt and a pair of fishing pliers lie beside the tray; behind, out of focus, mangroves and an orange sun on green water.

a white fiberglass flats skiff with a center console and a single outboard engine tied by bow and stern lines to a small weathered wooden dock in front of red mangroves, seen three-quarters from the bow in early morning light; a red triangular channel marker on a piling stands in the water beyond it and a brown pelican sits on a dock post; the hull, the cleats, the coiled dock line and the reflections in the calm green water are all drawn in fine detail.

a redfish (copper-bronze scales, white belly, one black spot at the base of the tail) lying on a wet white fish-measuring board on the deck of a skiff, seen from above, its closed mouth against the upright stop at the left end and a pair of wet hands gently pinching its tail at the other; the board's ruler marks are plain tick lines with no numbers. Above the board an open cooler full of crushed ice, and along the right edge the clear green river with mangrove roots, so the picture asks: keep it, or let it go. Every scale, drop of water and reflection is carefully painted.

an underwater view in clear green shallow water over seagrass and a mangrove root, with three different Florida inshore fish swimming left in a loose line, each painted with field-guide accuracy and fine scale detail: at the top a spotted seatrout (slim, silver-gray, many small black spots on the back, dorsal fin and tail); in the middle a redfish (copper-bronze, blunt nose, one black spot at the base of the tail); at the bottom a snook (long silver body, olive back, protruding lower jaw, one bold thin black stripe from gill to tail, yellowish fins). Sunlight ripples down through the water.

the helm of a flats skiff seen from just behind the steering wheel at sunrise: on the center console a folded nautical chart, a pair of polarized sunglasses, an open tackle tray and a fishing rod standing in a rod holder; beyond the bow a calm mangrove river with an orange sun coming up, a heron on a far point and a channel marker in the distance. The stainless wheel, the gauges with blank faces, the wet deck and the reflections are painted in fine detail. A feeling of the first morning of school, on the water.

a well-used spiral-bound field manual with a blank weathered canvas cover lying on the console of a flats skiff beside a pair of over-ear headphones, a guide's long-billed cap and a neatly coiled dock line by a steel cleat; beyond the low windshield a mangrove river at sunrise, the orange sun low over the water and a heron on a root. The worn corners of the manual, the stitching on the cap and the water drops on the deck are painted in fine detail. A feeling of the first day on the job as a fishing guide's mate.
